syllabus_topics: Introduction and review: Density functions and usual distributions (continuous and discrete)
Chi-2, t-Student, and F-Fisher distributions
Sample of a distribution
Programming in R: Introduction
Programming in R: Type of data
Programming in R: Read data from files
Programming in R: Application to statistics: type of distributions
Programming in R: Program flow control. Creation of functions
Statistical inference: test of difference of means, analysis of variance type I: Confidence intervals for mean and variance
Statistical inference: null hypothesis and p-value
Statistical inference: One-tailed and two-tailed t-tests
Statistical inference: Paired t-tests
Statistical inference: ANOVA type I
Simple linear regression: Least squares resolution
Simple linear regression: Statistical distributions of the estimated regression parameters
Simple linear regression: Inference in linear regression. Statistical distribution of regression estimates
Simple linear regression: Comparison with the test of difference of means and analysis of variance
Multiple linear regression (Linear models): Design matrix and matrix of contrasts
Multiple linear regression (Linear models): Influence of each factor
Multiple linear regression (Linear models): Explained variance and significance of the regression
teaching_methods: Continuous assessment through theoretical and practical tests
Learning to program fluently in R
Individual problem solving for proposed problems
Optional group work: analyzing a different dataset and applying statistical methods
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated based on a partial exam (35%) and a final exam (65%). For the extraordinary call, the final exam accounts for 100% of the grade. Both exams are written and include questions on statistical analysis in R. Any attempt at fraud, copying, or plagiarism is considered a serious infraction.
bibliography: Biostatistics with R: An Introduction to Statistics Through Biological Data, by Babak Shahbaba.
Introduction to Data Analysis and Graphical Presentation in Biostatistic with R: Statistic in the Large, by Thomas W. McFarland.
Other free electronic books, list available at http://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/170/free-statistical-textbooks.
